paper.title: DAPPER Leiomyosarcoma: Correlation and Survival Analysis of Radiomic, Microbiome and Clinical Data (Code Ocean capsule 3894632)

findings.evidence: Post-baseline covariates (deep_checks.py): Best.Response.RECISTv1, Gr1.Gr2.Toxicities, Gr3.Toxicities are measured during or after treatment but enter the survival models (surv_object_OS, surv_object_PFS) as baseline predictors. A patient must survive long enough to have a best response or a toxicity grade (immortal-time / outcome-dependent covariate), so their hazard ratios are biased toward benefit.

Rmd outputs (deep_checks.py): os_results computed in chunk(s) 0verall-Survival but never printed or written; the knitted output (capsule-3894632/dp_survival.nb.html, capsule-3894632/results/dp_survival.nb.html) can only hold what is printed: pfs_results. The stored result for os_results is therefore not in the materials.

Column trace (deep_checks.py): capsule-3894632/data/results/reduced-feature-set.csv has 41 columns after the code's own drops (line 20: features <- features[-1]); the model formulas use 39. Never modelled: Age, Gender. Steps: line 21: covariates <- colnames(features); line 22: covariates <- covariates[-1]; line 40: univ_formulas <- sapply(covariates[2:length(covariates)], function(x) as.formula(paste('surv_object_OS~', x))). Outcomes: surv_object_OS, surv_object_PFS.

Multiverse over four analysis choices (covariate set, PFS definition RECIST v1 vs iRECIST, multiplicity correction FDR/Bonferroni/none, post-baseline covariates included/excluded): the claim 'at least one feature is associated with PFS after multiplicity correction' holds in 12/24 universes (50%). The only breaking change is post_baseline=exclude: with baseline covariates only, no feature reaches adjusted p<0.05 in any of the 12 universes (mean number of significant features 0.0 vs 2.0). Covariate set, PFS definition and multiplicity method do not change the verdict.

The notebook computes os_results (univariate Cox for Overall Survival) but never prints it; the knitted notebook results/dp_survival.nb.html contains only the printed pfs_results table (39 rows). The README states that two dataframes, for OS and PFS, are generated, but the stored output contains no OS table, so the OS claim (C3) cannot be checked against any stored result.

The loop tests covariates[2:length(covariates)] after features[-1] and covariates[-1], i.e. 40 covariates (Gender ... Microbiome_RELA_s__Proteobacteria_bacterium_CAG_139; Age is dropped). The printed pfs_results has 39 rows and no Gender row, so the stored table does not contain every model the code fits. Our Python port (bp_out/port_PFS_results.csv) returns 40 rows including Gender (beta -0.25, p 0.20).

Best response (RECIST v1) and treatment-emergent toxicities are measured after treatment start, yet they enter the same univariate Cox models as baseline covariates (Age, Gender, Race, ECOG, Diagnosis, Treatment Arm) with no landmark or time-dependent formulation. The three post-baseline variables are the only ones with FDR-adjusted p<0.05 in the stored PFS table (Best Response p.adjust 0.021, Gr3 p.adjust 0.021, Gr1Gr2 p.adjust 0.038); all 36 baseline/radiomic/microbiome covariates have p.adjust>=0.68. Immortal-time bias can inflate these associations.

Claim 'At least one clinical, radiomic or microbiome feature is associated with progression-free survival after multiplicity correction (FDR-adjusted p<0.05)' holds in 50% of 24 universes. Single changes that flip it: post_baseline=exclude.
